The question

Onboarding touches more than one desk. How do you see it from all of them?

You'll learn how to

  • Sign in to Playgrounds, find Apps and Kanban, and see who's playable in this session

Phase 1

Enter Playgrounds

In this phase, you'll sign in to Playgrounds, find Apps and Kanban, and see who's playable in this session.

Pattern

Playable personas

Playgrounds is home to one simulated company, Cardboard Brands. What you see, which boards, which tickets, depends entirely on whose seat you're sitting in. Switching persona is how you check a recipe's output against the system it actually wrote to.

1.1

Enter Playgrounds

Every lab this week starts the same way: a fresh seat in Playgrounds, home to Cardboard Brands, the simulated company you'll be working in all day. Before you touch a ticket, you need to get in and see who you're allowed to be.

Overview

Sign in to Playgrounds, find your way to Apps and Kanban, and look at who's playable in this session.

Detailed steps 5 steps

This task is just orientation: signed in, apps found, one board opened. Task 2.1 uses what you find here to compare two specific seats side by side.

  • Go to https://playgrounds.training.workatolabs.com/ and sign in with your pseudonym, session code, and password — for example, azure-falcon / workspace-6 / kettle-violet-47. Double-check the credentials assigned to you for this session before signing in.
  • Click the 9-dot grid icon in the top bar to open Apps.
  • Click into Kanban. Kanban is our ticketing board for HR and IT. Which boards you can open depends on who's playing.
  • Max Rue sees two board cards here, Sam Chen sees only one. You'll compare what each one can actually do in the next task.
  • Use the persona switcher in the top bar to browse who's playable in this session.
Verify you're signed in, you can name at least three personas playable in this session, and you can say which app is Playgrounds' ticket tracker.
Phase 2

Browse the personas

In this phase, you'll see the same onboarding work from two different desks: IT and HR.

Pattern

Same ticket, different desk

A recipe's job report tells you it ran. The board each persona actually works from shows you what it produced, and that can look different depending on whose seat you're sitting in.

2.1

Browse the personas

Onboarding doesn't run through one person. IT provisions hardware, HR tracks the paperwork, and every one of those desks is a real seat in Playgrounds, not only a name on a ticket.

Overview

Look at the same kind of onboarding work from two different seats: Sam Chen, IT Admin, who owns asset requests, access provisioning, and collaboration-tool setup; and Max Rue, who owns the HR side of the same onboarding.

Detailed steps 4 steps

Later labs ask AIRO to explain and fix recipes that read and write to these boards. Knowing what those boards actually look like, from the people who work them, not only as a recipe's output, gives you a way to check AIRO's explanation against what's actually there.

  • As Sam Chen (IT Admin), open IT Support Kanban and look at the tickets being sent his way. Right now it starts off almost empty — you'll start your recipe later to sync in the tickets.
  • Click on a ticket to review what it looks like: description, assignee, reporter, priority, and any comments.
  • Switch to Max Rue (HR Analyst) and open HR Kanban to see the same kind of onboarding work from HR's side. Max Rue can also open IT Support as a guest, to check the IT ticket tied to the same onboarding, just not write or update it.
  • If a persona has more than one Kanban board visible to them, click the dropdown arrow next to the board name to switch between them.
Verify you can name which boards each persona can open (IT Support only for Sam Chen; HR Kanban and IT Support for Max Rue), and what IT Support is tracking: asset, access, and collaboration tickets.

Reflect

Before you open the project assigned to you in Lab 2, consider what you saw.

  • IT and HR are tracking the same onboarding from two different boards. Does any of the ticket detail look incorrect?
  • A recipe's job report tells you it ran. A ticket board shows the output. Check the job report if you want to debug any tickets later.

Wrap-up

Playgrounds isn't a mockup you click through once. It's home to Cardboard Brands, the company underneath every recipe you'll touch today, one seat at a time.

  • Whose desk, not only whose name. A ticket assigned to someone is only half real until you've seen their board.
  • The board is the record. AIRO's explanation and a recipe's job report both describe what happened, check the Kanban board for what actually got produced.
